If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecast to capture momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is near support, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid false breakout expectations.

If sentiment spikes from low to high within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 5 days to reflect sentiment volatility.

If sentiment is uniformly low (≤0.33) across 18 days, apply a 1.0–2.0% downward bias to all forecast points, especially late horizon, to reflect bearish consensus.

If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is near resistance, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid-horizon to prevent over-leverage on bullish momentum.
